name: Medicine and the drug
dimension: the clinical question asked of a disorder

objects.label: Disorders
objects.text: MD.O.A1 Disorders

objects.label: Disease entities
objects.text: MD.O.A1.1 Disease entities. A disorder is a departure from BI function that harms the person. The concept itself is debated in PL; MD uses a working definition.

objects.label: Immune disorders
objects.text: MD.O.A1.1.1 Immune disorders: autoimmunity, immunodeficiency, allergy. Normal immune function is BI.

objects.label: Neoplasms
objects.text: MD.O.A1.1.2 Neoplasms: the clinical entity is here; the cell biology is BI.

objects.label: Classification
objects.text: MD.O.A1.2 Classification. ICD-11 (in effect from 1 January 2022) and DSM-5-TR (2022). Classification rules are W12.

objects.label: Diagnostic thresholds, such as HbA1c for diabetes, are conventions set
objects.text: MD.O.A1.2.1 Diagnostic thresholds, such as HbA1c for diabetes, are conventions set by expert bodies.

objects.label: Mental disorder
objects.text: MD.O.A1.3 Mental disorder. The diagnosis is MD; normal cognition is MS; the concept of mental disorder is PL (CONTESTED).

objects.label: Categorical against dimensional models (RDoC, HiTOP) as competing clas
objects.text: MD.O.A1.3.1 Categorical against dimensional models (RDoC, HiTOP) as competing classification programmes.

objects.label: Syndromes and multimorbidity
objects.text: MD.O.A1.4 Syndromes and multimorbidity. Co-occurring conditions; frailty.

objects.label: Causes and mechanisms
objects.text: MD.O.A2 Causes and mechanisms

objects.label: Pathogens
objects.text: MD.O.A2.1 Pathogens. Germ theory. Koch's postulates are a historical heuristic, not a test for all pathogens (asymptomatic carriers and unculturable agents fail them).

objects.label: Antimicrobial resistance
objects.text: MD.O.A2.1.1 Antimicrobial resistance: selection under drug exposure (the evolutionary mechanism is BI).

objects.label: Genetic causes
objects.text: MD.O.A2.2 Genetic causes. Monogenic disorders with Mendelian inheritance; polygenic risk scores, whose predictive power varies by ancestry.

objects.label: Pathophysiology
objects.text: MD.O.A2.3 Pathophysiology. The mechanism of a disordered process (e.g. atherosclerosis, insulin resistance).

objects.label: Environmental and social determinants
objects.text: MD.O.A2.4 Environmental and social determinants. Exposures (tobacco, air pollution); deprivation. The social structure is MS; the exposure source is EV.

objects.label: Diagnosis and prognosis
objects.text: MD.O.A3 Diagnosis and prognosis

objects.label: Signs, symptoms and tests
objects.text: MD.O.A3.1 Signs, symptoms and tests. Clinical examination, imaging, laboratory tests.

objects.label: Test accuracy
objects.text: MD.O.A3.2 Test accuracy. Sensitivity and specificity. Predictive values depend on prevalence (Bayes' theorem, owned by MA.O.A5).

objects.label: Likelihood ratios combine with pre-test odds to give post-test odds, a
objects.text: MD.O.A3.2.1 Likelihood ratios combine with pre-test odds to give post-test odds, assuming test independence.

objects.label: Prognosis
objects.text: MD.O.A3.3 Prognosis. Survival, course, prognostic models. A model's calibration and discrimination are stated in a named population.

objects.label: Screening tests
objects.text: MD.O.A3.4 Screening tests. Testing people without symptoms. The programme decision is A5.3.

objects.label: Treatment and drugs
objects.text: MD.O.A4 Treatment and drugs

objects.label: Pharmacology
objects.text: MD.O.A4.1 Pharmacology. Pharmacokinetics: absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion. Pharmacodynamics: dose–response. The molecule is CH.

objects.label: First-order elimination
objects.text: MD.O.A4.1.1 First-order elimination: half-life t½ = ln 2 / k, for linear kinetics.

objects.label: Therapeutic index as the ratio of toxic to effective dose.
objects.text: MD.O.A4.1.2 Therapeutic index as the ratio of toxic to effective dose.

objects.label: Pharmacogenomics
objects.text: MD.O.A4.1.3 Pharmacogenomics: genotype-dependent drug response.

objects.label: Surgery and procedures.
objects.text: MD.O.A4.2 Surgery and procedures.

objects.label: Psychological and rehabilitative therapy
objects.text: MD.O.A4.3 Psychological and rehabilitative therapy. Cognitive behavioural therapy; physiotherapy. The mental mechanism is MS.

objects.label: Drug safety
objects.text: MD.O.A4.4 Drug safety. Adverse effects; pharmacovigilance after approval.

objects.label: Residues of veterinary drugs in human food
objects.text: MD.O.A4.4.1 Residues of veterinary drugs in human food: the safety limit is MD; the animal treatment is AG.

objects.label: Drug development and regulation
objects.text: MD.O.A4.5 Drug development and regulation. Trial phases I–IV; approval by bodies such as Medsafe (NZ), the FDA and EMA. The legal authority is LA.

objects.label: Populations and prevention
objects.text: MD.O.A5 Populations and prevention

objects.label: Epidemiology
objects.text: MD.O.A5.1 Epidemiology. Incidence, prevalence, relative and absolute risk.

objects.label: Transmission
objects.text: MD.O.A5.2 Transmission. R0 holds for a fully susceptible population under a stated contact model. The herd-immunity threshold 1 − 1/R0 assumes homogeneous mixing.

objects.label: Prevention and screening programmes
objects.text: MD.O.A5.3 Prevention and screening programmes. Vaccines; screening. Lead-time and length bias are stated defeaters for screening benefit.

objects.label: Health systems
objects.text: MD.O.A5.4 Health systems. Delivery, access and quality. Price and finance are EC; law is LA; policy is PO.

objects.label: Global and Māori health
objects.text: MD.O.A5.5 Global and Māori health. Health inequities by population. Under the two-mode rule, the tradition-internal side of rongoā and hauora is IK. Its clinical efficacy for a named condition is MD under W3.

warrants.standard: causal identification (Mendelian randomisation, natural experiments); mechanism shown
accuracy study against a reference standard (STARD)
pre-registered, adequately powered RCT (CONSORT); post-marketing surveillance
warrants.defeaters: surrogate endpoints, publication bias, short follow-up

sections.governing_thought:
Medicine is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges.
Its objects divide into five clinical questions: disorders, causes and mechanisms, diagnosis and prognosis, treatment and drugs, and populations and prevention.
sections.key_line:
Dimension: **the clinical question asked of a disorder.** Logic inductive. Order: the clinical sequence.
1. Disorders
2. Causes and mechanisms
3. Diagnosis and prognosis
4. Treatment and drugs
5. Populations and prevention

**MECE test.** "Type 2 diabetes is defined by HbA1c ≥ 48 mmol/mol" is A1 (a classification rule, W12). "Insulin resistance drives it" is A2. "HbA1c has sensitivity s" is A3. "Metformin lowers HbA1c" is A4. "Prevalence is rising" is A5.
sections.assignment_rules:
1. Normal function is BI; the disorder is MD.
2. The molecule is CH; its action in a patient is MD.
3. A cost-effectiveness claim is EC; the effect size it uses is MD.
4. Consent, liability and regulatory authority are LA. The ethics argument is PL.
5. An animal disorder is AG; a zoonosis's human side is MD.
6. A diagnostic test's mathematics is MA; its accuracy in a population is MD.
7. Rongoā and hauora: tradition-internal claims are IK; efficacy for a named condition is MD under W3.

sections.crosswalk:
**MeSH** has 16 top-level categories (A–N, V, Z).
- **Land (5):** C Diseases → A1; D Chemicals and drugs → A4.1; E Techniques → Face M and A3–A4; F Psychiatry and psychology → A1.3, A4.3; N Health care → A5.4.
- **Refused (11):**
  - A Anatomy → BI
  - B Organisms → BI
  - G Phenomena and processes → BI, CH
  - H Disciplines → bridges
  - I Anthropology, education, sociology → MS, ED
  - J Technology, industry, agriculture → EN, AG
  - K Humanities → AR, HI
  - L Information science → IS
  - M Named groups → substrate
  - V Publication characteristics → not a claim
  - Z Geographicals → substrate

Coverage: 5 of 16 land.

**ICD-11** (in effect from 1 January 2022) has chapters 1–26; chapter 26 is the supplementary chapter on traditional medicine conditions. Section V (functioning) and section X (extension codes) are not chapters.
- All disorder chapters land in A1.2.
- Chapter 26 lands in A1.2 with a CONTESTED flag.
- V and X are refused as cells. Functioning goes to A5.4 and A3; extension codes are W12 conventions.

**ANZSRC 32** (16 groups) and **42** (9 groups) (checked 9 Oct 2026, ABS anzsrc2020_for.xlsx):
- 32: 3201–3215 clinical and biomedical groups land in A1–A4. 3204 Immunology, 3208 Medical physiology and 3209 Neurosciences split with BI and MS. 3210 Nutrition and dietetics splits with AG. 3299 Other is not a cell.
- 42: 4202 Epidemiology and 4206 Public health → A5. 4203 Health services and systems → A5.4. 4201 Allied health, 4204 Midwifery and 4205 Nursing → B.C7. 4207 Sports science → BI and MS. 4208 Traditional, complementary and integrative medicine → A4 under W3, CONTESTED. 4299 Other is not a cell.
- Coverage: 23 of 23 substantive groups land, wholly or in part.
sections.validation:
Sizes: key line 5. Face O 5 cells + 22 sub-cells = 27. M roles 5. Heuristics 6, outside the count. W rows 5. B bridges 9.
Key line, word for word: Disorders. Causes and mechanisms. Diagnosis and prognosis. Treatment and drugs. Populations and prevention.
CONTESTED: the concept of mental disorder (MD vs PL vs MS); categorical vs dimensional classification; traditional medicine in ICD-11 chapter 26 and ANZSRC 4208.
OPEN: mechanisms of many chronic diseases (e.g. Alzheimer's disease); the transportability of polygenic scores across ancestries.
